headline: WordPress Core RCE enters KEV as a $6bn crypto heist and a blood-bank intrusion land
standfirst: CISA's confirmation that an unauthenticated WordPress Core race condition is being exploited in the wild leads a day otherwise dominated by breaches: altered refrigeration settings at a French blood service, a nine-figure bank theft traced to a supplier, and Binance's own account of a fake-interview malware chain.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

CISA added CVE-2026-119977, a WordPress Core TOCTOU race condition, to its KEV catalog citing evidence of active exploitation [[s36]]. Scored 8.1 HIGH (CWE-367), it stems from predictable, web-accessible staging paths used during full-package core upgrades, and the NVD description says unauthenticated attackers can execute code on the server during the upgrade window. The vector is network-reachable with no privileges or user interaction required, but high attack complexity — exploitation depends on hitting an upgrade in progress, not a fire-and-forget request. Supplied affected ranges run from 4.7 through the 6.6 branch, each with its own fixed release; the description's reference to versions up to 7.1.3 does not match those ranges, so verify against the vendor advisory. CISA's required action cites BOD 26-04 and forensics triage guidance, with a due date that binds federal agencies only. Analysis: for a platform this ubiquitous, KEV status moves this from the monthly patch cycle to this week, and upgrade logs are worth a look.

## Breaches

France's national blood service said a cyberattack on a refrigeration equipment provider altered temperature and defrost settings at three facilities, threatening stored blood products [[s3]]. The intrusion reached into physical safety controls rather than data, which is the part worth escalating internally.

Binance attributes an approximately $6.34 billion theft to North Korean hackers who used a fake job interview to get an employee to install malware, then compromised wallet infrastructure [[s43]]. The transferable detail is the path: recruiting pipeline to engineer endpoint to custody systems.

Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirmed attackers made transfers using the bank's own accounts after compromising an unnamed supplier, with an estimated $133 million taken [[s2]]. Third-party access converging with transfer authority, again.

## Vulnerabilities

Two Xen flaws let a malicious guest VM read and write the memory of other guests on the same host, including dom0 [[s25]]. Patches are out, every version from 4.6 onward is affected, and the project says there is no known mitigation; no CVE identifiers appear in the supplied excerpt, so track fixes through the advisory. Hypervisor isolation is the assumption much else rests on.

Ruby on Rails fixed a critical Active Storage flaw that let an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files to an app's server via a crafted upload where ImageMagick processes files, with fixes in 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2 [[s24]]. Anyone piping user uploads through ImageMagick should treat this as immediate work.

## Research

Researchers attribute a large-scale watering-hole campaign to APT29-linked activity, using compromised sites, fake domains and a supply-chain compromise of a Ukrainian web analytics service, with injected JavaScript harvesting browser and device attributes before serving iOS and Android exploits [[s14]]. The attribution is theirs and should be read as such; the mechanism — analytics script as delivery vehicle — is the durable lesson.

## Industry

Google disrupted the XCPE botnet, saying it had grown to 1.3 million devices — set-top boxes and IoT gear backdoored into criminal infrastructure — and alleges manufacturer Videostrong ran the operation [[s7]]. Consumer IoT defaults keep seeding other people's botnets; accountability for that is the story.
